title: Straightforward CRUD should not be escalated into rich domain architecture
task: Review a proposal to add aggregates, value objects, domain services, repository interfaces, and use-case classes to a small CRUD module.
context: The module stores and retrieves profile preferences.
Validation is limited to field shape, authorization, and a few range checks.
There are no meaningful state transitions or cross-entity business invariants.
evidence: Existing code maps HTTP input to validated data and performs direct persistence operations.
The proposed layers mostly forward the same values unchanged.
No bug or maintenance problem is tied to missing domain abstractions.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Adopt DDD because all business applications should have a domain layer.
Create repository interfaces for hypothetical future databases.
Wrap every primitive field in a value object regardless of invariant value.
expected_decision_properties: Keep the design simple and explicit unless real domain complexity appears.
Preserve meaningful validation, authorization, and persistence boundaries without adding pass-through layers.
State that source-specific DDD guidance remains research-gated and is not needed to justify simplicity here.
Provide concrete revisit triggers such as growing invariants or lifecycle complexity.
unacceptable_reasoning: A database-backed application is automatically a complex domain.
More domain layers always improve maintainability.
Simple CRUD is an architectural smell.
expected_tradeoffs: present simplicity vs speculative domain extensibility
verification_expectations: Run current API and persistence tests.
Verify authorization and validation remain explicit.
Check repository history for evidence of repeated domain-rule changes before adding new abstractions.
revisit_when: Cross-field or cross-entity invariants become non-trivial.
Business policy becomes duplicated across multiple entry points.
notes: Complements the existing Python layering case with language-neutral domain-complexity routing.
